title: Performance guards that count work instead of timing it
note: R49: the scheduler-readiness guard counts job records examined, policy evaluations and history re-hashes per ready_queue call; each mutation plants a regression a wall-clock ratio could only have caught on a quiet machine.

mutations.name: PC1_readiness_rescans_the_queue_per_job
mutations.replace:
self.in_flight_resources()
            if not self.readiness(job, at_seq=seq, resolve=resolve,
mutations.rationale: R49: the ready queue becomes quadratic in the queue length, and only a clock would have seen it

mutations.name: PC2_the_ready_queue_rereads_history
mutations.find:
seq = self.at_seq() if at_seq is None else at_seq
        out = []
mutations.replace:
seq = self.at_seq() if at_seq is None else at_seq
        self.log.verify()
        out = []
mutations.rationale: R49: every ready-queue query re-verifies the whole history

mutations.name: PC3_a_hidden_scan_of_the_job_map_per_job
mutations.rationale: R49: a per-job scan of the job map hidden after the readiness check

mutations.name: PC4_a_lookup_lists_its_fanout_directory
mutations.replace: rel = next(f"{dg[:_FANOUT]}/{n}" for n in os.listdir(self.root / dg[:_FANOUT]) if n == dg[_FANOUT:])
mutations.rationale: a lookup that confirms the blob by listing its fan-out directory: the cost grows with the store, which the clock could only guess at

mutations.name: PC5_a_lookup_searches_the_whole_store
mutations.replace: rel = next(p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() for p in self.root.glob(f"*/{dg[_FANOUT:]}"))
mutations.rationale: a lookup that searches every bucket for the name instead of deriving the path
